title: Spreading and descending nonreduced fibres through a universal homeomorphism
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $U\subseteq Y$ be an open subscheme, let $T$ be an irreducible scheme [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and let $q:T\to U$ be a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Give $T$ its $Y$-scheme structure via the composite $T\xrightarrow{q}U\hookrightarrow Y$. Set $P=X\times_YT$ with projection $h:P\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose the fibre $P_\xi$ is not reduced [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $W\subseteq T$ such that $P_t$ is not reduced for every $t\in W$, and $V=q(W)\subseteq U\subseteq Y$ is nonempty and open in $Y$ with $X_y$ not geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$ for every $y\in V$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Tag 0577 (lemma-not-geometrically-reduced-in-neighbourhood), proof: application of the nonreduced-fibre neighbourhood theorem and descent of the resulting open under the base homeomorphism

proof.text: Let $r:T\to Y$ be the given composite. Since finite type means locally of finite type and quasi-compact, $f$ has both properties. Apply locally-finite-type base change and quasi-compact base change to $f$ along $r$. The projection $h:X\times_YT\to T$ has both properties, hence is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), including the proof using schemes.tex Tag 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change)

proof.text: Apply the nonreduced-generic-fibre neighbourhood theorem to $h:P\to T$. Its hypotheses hold: $h$ is of finite type by Step 1, $T$ is irreducible with generic point $\xi$ by assumption, and $P_\xi$ is nonreduced by assumption. It gives a nonempty open $W\subseteq T$ with $P_t$ nonreduced for every $t\in W$.

For $t\in W$, set $y=q(t)\in U\subseteq Y$. The morphism $r$ induces a field homomorphism $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(t)$. By the definitions of fibre and fibre product, $$P_t=(X\times_YT)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\cong X_y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t).$$ Explicitly, maps from any test scheme $S$ to either side are exactly pairs $(a:S\to X,b:S\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t))$ with $f a=r\,i_t b$, where $i_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$ is canonical; composing $b$ with the residue-field map supplies the required map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$. These descriptions give inverse maps by uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property. If $X_y$ were geometrically reduced, its base change along the field extension $\kappa(t)/\kappa(y)$ would be reduced by definition. This contradicts Step 2. Thus $X_y$ is not geometrically reduced.

source.place: Tag 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced), first sentence of proof, and Tag 0577, final sentence; only the defining implication of geometric reducedness is needed

proof.text: Base changing the universal homeomorphism $q$ along $\mathrm{id}_U$ shows directly from its definition that $q:T\to U$ is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces. Therefore $V=q(W)=(q^{-1})^{-1}(W)$ is open in $U$ and is nonempty because $W$ is nonempty. As $U$ is open in $Y$, $V$ is open in $Y$. For each $y\in V$, the definition of image gives $t\in W$ with $q(t)=y$; Step 3 then says that $X_y$ is not geometrically reduced. This $W$ and $V$ have every required property.
